answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks therefore finds them worthless when it returns to them. The tundra decay curve is applied at each close, karst records the drop, and plume recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 4 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That is 621 dollars of sunk cost for a share worth less than the deposit itself. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
